question.problem:
Consider the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡4x=1$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are written in **ascending order**, what are their values? Express your answers in terms of $\pi .$

${x}_{1}=${{field-1}}$,\,$
${x}_{2}=${{field-2}}$,\,$
${x}_{3}=${{field-3}}$,\,$
${x}_{4}=${{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{n\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{8}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{8}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{9\pi }{8}$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{13\pi }{8}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{8},\frac{5\pi }{8},\frac{9\pi }{8},\frac{13\pi }{8}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{8},\,{x}_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{8},\,{x}_{3}=\frac{9\pi }{8},\,{x}_{4}=\frac{13\pi }{8}
$$
